'''Jasim Uddin Ahmed''' (1 January 1933 – 21 September 2022) was a [[Bangladeshi]] language activist, nuclear physicist, poet and author. He received the [[Ekushey Padak]] award in 2016 for his contribution to the [[Bengali language movement|Language Movement]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://moca.portal.gov.bd/sites/default/files/files/moca.portal.gov.bd/page/7e22de29_5250_4bed_bd62_a032ea740a55/Ekushe%20Padak%20list%20up%20to%2018.pdf|script-title=bn:একুশে পদকপ্রাপ্ত সুধীবৃন্দ|accessdate=16 January 2020|language=bn|website=Ministry of Cultural Affairs|archive-date=5 January 2020|archive-url=https://archive.today/20200105102005/https://moca.portal.gov.bd/sites/default/files/files/moca.portal.gov.bd/page/7e22de29_5250_4bed_bd62_a032ea740a55/Ekushe%20Padak%20list%20up%20to%2018.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Biography==
Ahmed was born on 1 January 1933 in [[Galiarchar]], [[Daudkandi Upazila|Daudkandi]] of [[Comilla District|Comilla]].<ref name=a>{{cite news |url=http://www.bhorerkagoj.com/print-edition/2015/02/05/17498.php|script-title=bn:কানের পাশ দিয়ে বেশ কয়েকটি গুলি ব্যারাকের বারান্দায় বাঁশের চালায় বিঁধে গেল|date=5 February 2015|access-date=16 January 2020|newspaper=Bhorer Kagoj|language=bn|archive-date=16 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200116102554/http://www.bhorerkagoj.com/print-edition/2015/02/05/17498.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was an integral part of the  [[Bengali language movement|Language Movement]] while a student at [[Dhaka University]]. He was on the front line of the protest rallies on 21 February 1952.  During these demonstrations, the police opened fire on the crowd, and [[Abul Barkat]], who was standing beside him, was fatally shot.<ref name=a/>

Ahmed started his academic career at [[Dhaka College]] in 1956 before moving to the [[United States]] for his M.S. at the [[University of Rochester]], and his [[Ph.D.]] at the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name=b/>  He joined the [[Atomic Energy Centre, Dhaka]] in 1963 and moved to the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] in Vienna, Austria in 1970.<ref name=b/> He eventually became the head of the Nuclear Radiation Security Department of the institution. He retired from the post in 1994.<ref name=b>{{cite news
|url=https://m.bdnews24.com/bn/detail/bangladesh/1102880
|script-title=bn:হায়াৎ মামুদ, তোয়াব খান, শাহীন সামাদসহ ১৬ জন পাচ্ছেন একুশে পদক
|date=10 February 2015
|access-date=16 January 2020
|work=bdnews24.com
|language=bn
|archive-date=16 January 2020
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200116102554/https://m.bdnews24.com/bn/detail/bangladesh/1102880
|url-status=dead
}}</ref>

Ahmed has written about 36 books,<ref name=b/> and received the [[Ekushey Padak]] in 2016 for his contribution to the [[Bengali language movement|Language Movement]]. He made a special appearance on a television drama titled ''Noishobdo Joddha'' which was broadcast on 19 February 2016 on [[ATN Bangla]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.jagonews24.com/m/entertainment/news/79849
|script-title=bn:নিভৃতচারী ভাষা সৈনিককে নিয়ে নৈশব্দ যোদ্ধা
|date=9 February 2016|access-date=16 January 2020|work=Jagonews24.com|language=bn
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
|url=https://www.bhorerkagoj.com/print-edition/2016/02/10/74742.php
|script-title=bn:মাতৃভাষা দিবসে অর্ষার 'নৈশব্দ যোদ্ধা'
|date=10 February 2016
|access-date=16 January 2020
|newspaper=Bhorer Kagoj
|language=bn
|archive-date=16 January 2020
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200116102551/https://www.bhorerkagoj.com/print-edition/2016/02/10/74742.php
|url-status=dead
}}</ref>

== Death ==
Ahmed died on 21 September 2022 in [[Bangkok Hospital]], Thailand.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jasim Uddin Ahmed dies |url=https://www.newagebd.net/article/181825/jasim-uddin-ahmed-dies |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=New Age |language=en}}</ref>
